newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-SUSPENDED DE BILDE APOLOGISES FOR PUNCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SUSPENDED DE BILDE APOLOGISES FOR PUNCH.

text.p: Disgraced Belgium striker Gilles De Bilde, who punched Krist Porte in the face during a match last month, publicly apologised to his victim and fans in a prime-time television show.
"I hope you'll forgive me," the Anderlecht striker told BRTN in a taped interview on Wednesday evening during the Belgium player of the year ceremony.

"I gathered my last bit of courage to say: 'Krist, I never intended to hit you like this and every moment of the day I think of the pain you must go through and the uncertainty about your soccer future that I caused'," De Bilde said.
De Bilde was charged with assault and grievous bodily harm after striking the Aalst player during the game on December 21. Porte suffered a broken eye socket and nose.
De Bilde spent a night in jail after the incident and has been suspended until further notice both by his club and the Belgian soccer union.
De Bilde, looking pale and drawn, also apologised to fellow players and fans. "I know I went way out of line," he said in his first public statements since the incident.
"I deserve a punishment," said De Bilde, who added he was hoping to get another chance and wished Porte a swift recovery.
Porte still suffers from blurred vision and severe headaches and has to rest for at least three more weeks before undergoing any further treatment.
The 'golden boot' trophy for Belgium's best player of 1996 went to Club Brugge captain Franky Van der Elst.
